name: Angiocentric Glioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of monomorphous bipolar tumor cells arranged in an angiocentric pattern
MRI showing a well-demarcated, T2 hyperintense, non-enhancing cortical or subcortical lesion
Drug-resistant focal epilepsy or seizure onset in childhood or young adulthood
MYB-QKI gene fusion detected by molecular testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of angiocentric growth pattern with compatible MRI findings and clinical presentation of focal epilepsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for MYB-QKI fusion supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as focal epilepsy refractory to medication

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits related to lesion location
searchTerms: weakness or numbness matching lesion site
cortical or subcortical abnormality on MRI

common.symptomName: Seizure aura with sensory or motor symptoms
searchTerms: seizure warning with sensory or motor signs
sensory or movement symptoms before seizure
temporary weakness on one side after seizure

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances related to lesion location

searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain swelling
seizures spreading to full body convulsions

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to lesion mass effect
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain due to lesion

imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated, T2 hyperintense, non-enhancing cortical or subcortical lesion
Absence of significant mass effect or edema on imaging
other: Histopathology demonstrating angiocentric growth pattern with monomorphous bipolar cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and EMA dot-like positivity

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of floating neurons in mucinous pools
Typically presents with seizures but lacks angiocentric growth pattern
Different molecular profile without MYB-QKI fusion
Often cystic with mural nodule on imaging
Usually occurs in cerebellum or optic pathways

redFlags: New onset of generalized tonic-clonic seizures
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Wang M, et al. Angiocentric glioma: clinical and molecular features. Acta Neuropathol Commun. 2017.
Perry A, et al. Angiocentric glioma: a distinctive epilepsy-associated tumor with monomorphous bipolar cells and angiocentric growth pattern. Brain Pathol. 2005.
